To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Time Domain Parameters (1) outperform all band-power based features in the absence of subject-specific data and (2) are advantageous over band-power features when subject-specific data is available, but the subject's frequency content changes from calibration to feedback.

Time Domain Parameters are advantageous in both situations: 1. when the frequency content of a signal is unknown and no calibration is possible, 2. when a subject-specific calibration is possible, but the subject's brain state changes when the feedback is introduced.
Time Domain Parameters can be used as a feature in EEG-based Brain- Computer Interfaces and that they outperform all band powers tested in the present study.
